title: Uniqueness of the global orientation
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ and $\kappa(t)$ be as in
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The restriction of the
homomorphism group to
geometric points is an
injective map

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,\Lambda)}
\bigl(\Lambda_Y,Rs^!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\bigr)
\longrightarrow
\prod_{\bar y\to Y}H^2_{s(\bar y)}(\mathbf A^1_{\bar y},\Lambda(1)),
$$

whose image contains the family with every component $1\in\Lambda$ (by
[thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] and the normalization of
[thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]). Consequently
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ is the unique global morphism whose pullback to
every geometric point is the normalized class $1$.

proof.text:
Use the current [def-pur-conventions]: $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ is the finite coefficient ring, $A_Y$ is its degree-zero constant coefficient unit, and $Rs^!$ denotes the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] on the stated bounded constructible categories. The input $A_X(1)$ and the support object below are the finite-level objects of those conventions. Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $U=\mathbf G_{m,Y}$, $p:X\to Y$, $\pi=pj$, and $F=Rs^!A_X(1)[2]$. Use precisely [def-pur-affine-line-datum], including its present coefficient-level convention $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$ and the specified etale/pro-etale identification of the twist and Kummer class; no integral or rational coefficients are asserted here. The base is separated finite type over $k$, as assumed in the item. By [lem-pur-gysin-structure], $F\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ and $\mathcal H^i(F)=0$ for $i\ne0$. Put $L=\mathcal H^0(F)$. Applying [lem-pur-concentrated-complex-shift](1) with $r=0$ gives $F\simeq L[0]$. The fully faithful degree-zero embedding of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] therefore identifies
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(Y,A)}(A_Y,F)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_Y}(A_Y,L)=\Gamma(Y,L).$$
The last bijection sends a sheaf map to the image of $1$; its inverse sends a section $v$ to $a\mapsto av$, on every object of the site. This also explains why the Hom group is a module of global sections, not a rank-one sheaf or necessarily a rank-one module.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text:
We need the normalized boundary to trivialize $L$, not merely an unspecified lisse rank-one structure. Here is the unit's localization argument. Work first on ordinary etale sites with $B=A_X(1)^{\mathrm{et}}$. The zero section and open complement are those of the datum; $j$ is quasi-compact since locally its image is $D(t)$. By [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] there is the counit/unit triangle
$$s_*Rs^!B\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*B\longrightarrow .$$
Apply $Rp_*$, which carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Choose the small skeletons in [def-weil-size-convention]. The K-injective resolutions required there exist for these module-sheaf categories by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], with $ps=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $pj=\pi$, give
$$Rs^!B\longrightarrow Rp_*B\longrightarrow R\pi_*j^*B\longrightarrow Rs^!B[1].$$
To match this ordinary etale calculation with the current convention [def-pur-conventions], take the compactification $Y\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Y\xrightarrow{s}X$ of the zero section. Its etale compact-support functor is $Rs_*=s_*$: on the displayed affine charts $s$ is the finite cyclic quotient $R[t]\to R$, and [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] makes its direct image exact. Although that node is stated for abelian sheaves, its exactness applies to $A$-module sheaves: kernels and cokernels have the same underlying abelian sheaves, and forgetting the $A$-action commutes with direct image and reflects exactness. Thus the termwise module direct image preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes $Rs_*$ as well. Thus the ordinary etale adjoint $s^{\times}$ used in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the $Rs^!$ of the support triangle are right adjoints of the same $s_*$. Their natural Hom bijections identify them and their counits. The current convention gives the adjunction on the bounded constructible categories; the bounded-below finite-level formula in that definition provides the etale-origin comparison used here. No ambient pro-etale adjoint or additional exceptional-adjoint admissibility datum is needed. The same calculation therefore represents the chapter's support object: [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] defines its finite-level value by transport of the etale adjoint, and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives the required identity $R\nu_*\nu^*B=B$. The comparison in [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] applies to $p,j,\pi$ (all are quasi-compact and quasi-separated: over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$ their sources are $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$, and $j$ is the principal-open localization. These affine charts and their diagonals are spectra of rings, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]; this verifies the definitions of quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]) and is compatible with composites and input maps, while [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact] commutes with cohomology. More explicitly, the comparison isomorphisms identify the $\nu_Y^*$-images of the etale terms and their maps with the pro-etale terms and maps in [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer]. Exactness gives $\mathcal H^q(\nu_Y^*K)=\nu_Y^*\mathcal H^q(K)$. Full faithfulness reflects zero objects and isomorphisms: if $\nu_Y^*M=0$, its identity comes from $\mathrm{id}_M$ and faithfulness forces $M=0$; apply this to the kernel and cokernel to reflect an isomorphism of sheaves. Hence the vanishing and Kummer-generator isomorphism in that node hold on the etale models too. Applying the exact $\nu_Y^*$ to their long exact sequence gives the pro-etale calculation with the same input maps.
Take the long exact cohomology sequence by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]. The vanishing of $R^1p_*B$ and $R^2p_*B$ in [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer](1) makes its boundary
$$\delta:R^1\pi_*A(1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^2(Rs^!A_X(1))=L$$
an isomorphism. Clause (2) of that node supplies the isomorphism $A_Y\to R^1\pi_*A(1)$, $1\mapsto\kappa(t)$. Their composite $o:A_Y\to L$ is consequently an isomorphism. It is exactly $\mathcal H^0(\operatorname{pur}_s)$: the first arrow of the localization triangle is the counit, its connecting map is the support boundary, and [lem-pur-gysin-structure] and [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] define $\operatorname{pur}_s$ from that boundary. To check this last identification on global sections, the edge map sends the global class $\kappa(t)$ to its section in $R^1\pi_*A(1)$, by clause (2) of [prop-pur-gm-relative-kummer]. The connecting morphism $R\pi_*A(1)\to Rs^!A_X(1)[1]$ induces both the boundary on global cohomology and $\delta$ on cohomology sheaves. The edge maps are natural for this morphism, so $\delta$ of that section is the section corresponding to the global boundary $\partial\kappa(t)$. Thus the composite sends $1$ to precisely that section under the canonical identification of [lem-pur-gysin-structure]. This verifies the normalization of the sheaf isomorphism, rather than assuming an additional normalized Kummer datum.

proof.text:
Combining the degree-zero Hom identification of step 1 with $o^{-1}$ of step 2 identifies every $\varphi:A_Y\to F$ with a unique section $a\in\Gamma(Y,A_Y)$. Explicitly the endomorphism $m_a:A_Y\to A_Y$, $b\mapsto ab$, satisfies
$$\varphi=\operatorname{pur}_s\circ m_a.$$
Indeed both sides correspond to the sheaf map $o\circ m_a$ under the fully faithful single-complex embedding. The orientation corresponds to the section $1$. This is a calculation of sheaf maps on the degree-zero representatives, so it does not require a claim that geometric pullback is faithful on an arbitrary derived category.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $g:\bar y=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Let $h:\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}\to X$ and $s':\bar y\to\mathbf A^1_{\bar y}$ be the base changes. Under the natural supported-Hom description [lem-pur-supported-hom] and the etale-origin closed-immersion adjunction of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], restriction in the statement sends the transpose of a supported class to the transpose of its pullback; the supported pullback is the functoriality in the pair and the coefficient sheaf in [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. For completeness, if $\epsilon:s_*F\to A_X(1)[2]$ is the counit, the supported representative of $\varphi$ is $\epsilon\circ s_*\varphi$. With $\varphi=\operatorname{pur}_s\circ m_a$, it is $(\epsilon\circ s_*\operatorname{pur}_s)\circ s_*m_a$. Pullback carries this precomposition to precomposition by $s'_*g^*m_a$, using the canonical supported-source comparison. Here that comparison is natural in the sheaf on $Y$: on the etale models the zero section and its base change are finite (on affine charts they are the cyclic quotients $R[t]\to R$ and $\Omega[t]\to\Omega$). By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula], their pushforwards have the original stalk on the closed support and zero stalk off it. [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] identifies global sections of geometric inverse images with the corresponding stalks, so the canonical map $h^*s_*M\to s'_*g^*M$ is the identity on all these stalks and is an isomorphism by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]. Explicitly this comparison is adjoint under $s'^*\dashv s'_*$ to $s'^*h^*s_*M\cong g^*s^*s_*M\to g^*M$, where the last arrow is the pullback of the counit of $s^*\dashv s_*$. Naturality of this counit makes the comparison commute with every map $M\to M'$, in particular $m_a$. [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and the exact module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] make this also the comparison of the derived functors on the bounded-below etale models. The finite-level site comparisons in step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] give the supported-source comparison for the chapter's objects. In particular it is natural in $m_a$, which is all the calculation requires. Since $m_a$ is multiplication by a section, $g^*m_a$ is multiplication by its germ $a_{\bar y}\in A$. This is also seen by extending the multiplier to $p^*a$ on $X$; $s^*p^*a=a$ because $ps=\mathrm{id}$, and on the fibre $h^*p^*a$ is the constant scalar $a_{\bar y}$. Thus restriction on supported cohomology gives
$$r_{\bar y}(\varphi)=a_{\bar y}\,r_{\bar y}(\operatorname{pur}_s).$$
The ordinary finite-coefficient inverse image is exact and preserves constant coefficients by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the global sections of its value at a geometric point are the stalk by [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. For the chapter's pro-etale models the same formula follows from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and the specified comparison of the supported class. By [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation], $r_{\bar y}(\operatorname{pur}_s)$ is the normalized class, and [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation] gives the $A$-linear residue isomorphism $\rho_{\bar y}$ sending it to $1$. Therefore
$$\rho_{\bar y}\bigl(r_{\bar y}(\varphi)\bigr)=a_{\bar y}.$$
This argument only uses pullback of supported classes and its naturality; it does not assume that an exceptional-base-change mate is invertible or that $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is finite type over $k$.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text: Suppose $r_{\bar y}(\varphi)=r_{\bar y}(\psi)$ for every geometric point, and write $a,b\in\Gamma(Y,A_Y)$ for their sections in step 3. Step 4 gives $a_{\bar y}=b_{\bar y}$ everywhere. We justify the section test in the correct category. The constant sheaf $A_Y$ is the exact comparison pullback of its etale model, by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1),(2). Full faithfulness on $D^+$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], together with [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], identifies its pro-etale sheaf endomorphisms with its etale sheaf endomorphisms. These identifications respect geometric inverse image by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Let $f$ be the etale endomorphism corresponding to $m_a-m_b$. Its stalk maps are zero by step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk]. On underlying abelian sheaves put $I=\operatorname{im}f$. Exactness of etale geometric stalks [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives $I_{\bar y}=\operatorname{im}f_{\bar y}=0$. Applying [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to $0\to I$ gives $I=0$, hence $f=0$, hence $m_a=m_b$ and $a=b$. Step 3 then gives $\varphi=\psi$. This proves injectivity of the displayed restriction homomorphism. The test was made on etale sheaves and transported by full faithfulness; geometric stalks need not be conservative on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves.

source.place: Steps 1–4; expanded with the unit rank-one calculation

proof.text: The morphism $\operatorname{pur}_s$ exists by [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] and has every geometric component equal to the class corresponding to $1\in A$ under [thm-pur-rank-one-local-calculation]. Therefore the all-ones family lies in the image. If another morphism has these same components, injectivity from step 5 makes it equal to $\operatorname{pur}_s$. No connectedness of $Y$ was assumed: on a disconnected base sections can take different values on different components and the product tests each of them. If $Y$ is empty, its sheaf module category and the Hom group are zero and the empty product is the zero group, so the same assertion and uniqueness hold.
